clue.text: Forced to stick together by number of journalists in school

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word that follows, school here wrapping round them

parts.note: a coed is a coeducational school
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
the press is the collective name for journalists

explanation.surface: Reporters crammed into a school are squeezed together by sheer numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number of journalists' reads as one phrase, a headcount, but splits into two pieces; a coed is a coeducational school, taking both boys and girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Something compressed has been squeezed by pressure until its parts are packed tightly into a smaller space.

clue.text: A contrary answer?

parts.note: surface reading: a reply that is awkward or obstructive
setter's reading: a reply that contradicts itself, holding both opposites at once

explanation.walkthrough: Contrary usually means stubborn, but here it means containing its own opposite: an equivocal reply that says both things at once.
explanation.definitionFit: An equivocal response that neither commits to agreement nor refusal is self-contradictory, giving both opposite replies together.

clue.text: He cuts down, or follows a bizarre diet

indicators.note: follows tells us the first word comes after the scrambled piece in the answer
something bizarre is strange and out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man trims himself down, unless he takes up some odd eating regime instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts down' sounds like slimming, which fits the diet, but it means trimming text.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who prepares copy for publication shortens and trims writing, reducing articles to fit the available space.

clue.text: Fruity-sounding couple

indicators.note: sounding means we want a word that is said like a fruit, though spelt differently

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A rather fruity-voiced pair of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things or people taken together form a set of two, the same as a duo.

clue.text: Fashionable get-up judged to be complete

parts.note: in means in fashion

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
rated means assessed or judged

explanation.surface: A trendy outfit is judged to be the whole package.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get-up' looks like an outfit, but it splits into a word and its reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something integrated has all its parts combined into one whole, so it is unified and entire.

clue.text: Gail and Rose revamped the women's living quarters

indicators.note: to revamp is to renovate or remodel, so these letters are reworked into a new arrangement

parts.note: letters taken as written
letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Two women, Gail and Rose, have redecorated their shared rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the harem, the secluded part of a Muslim palace where wives and concubines lived.

clue.text: Join section, including the first part

indicators.note: including means one thing is held inside another

parts.note: a slice is a section or portion

indicators.note: the first means we keep only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: opening letter of part

explanation.surface: Instructions to attach a piece, beginning with the opening section.
explanation.definitionFit: To splice is to join two ends, as of rope or film, by interweaving or overlapping them.

clue.text: Pastry dish left inside to cool

indicators.note: inside means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to fan is to cool by moving air
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A tart is left in the kitchen to cool down.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a sweet or savoury filling, baked like a tart.

clue.text: Attracted to being settled when in debt

parts.note: a matter that is over is finished and settled
drawn means attracted

explanation.surface: Someone drawn to settling down just when they are short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces are joined in the reverse of the clue's order: the settled word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank account is overdrawn when more money has been taken out than was in it, leaving the holder owing.

clue.text: Kick out former sports student

parts.note: ex means former
PE is physical education, school sports
L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: An order to throw out someone who used to be a sports student.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to force someone out of a school or organisation, removing them permanently.

clue.text: Stir paste with both hands so it will stick

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
L and R, left and right hands

explanation.surface: Instructions to mix glue with both hands until it is tacky.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a sticking plaster, the British term for an adhesive bandage.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticking plaster is an adhesive dressing; plaster on walls also clings as it sets.

clue.text: Delight at having run away from family member

indicators.note: away from means a letter has gone missing from the following word

parts.note: a relation is a family member
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Joy at escaping from a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness and exhilaration, the same feeling as joy or delight.

clue.text: Church official is the type to branch out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lay officer in some churches
second meaning: a kind of tree, which grows branches

explanation.surface: A church officer with a habit of expanding his interests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branch out' sounds like a person trying new things, but it is literal: a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a senior lay leader in Presbyterian churches, and also a shrub or tree bearing elderberries.

clue.text: Found in the sea, where girl's broken free

parts.note: Coral is a girl's name

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl has escaped somewhere out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition describes the answer: a ridge built up from living marine organisms lies in warm shallow ocean water.

clue.text: Girl to clean teeth after sugary treat

parts.note: Candy is a girl's name
to floss is to clean between the teeth

explanation.surface: A girl brushes up on dental hygiene after eating sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Spun sugar on a stick is called cotton candy in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: This fairground confection is spun sugar wound into a fluffy mass, an obviously sweet indulgence.

clue.text: Kitchen equipment in need of oiling

definitions.text: Kitchen equipment in need of oiling

parts.note: surface reading: kitchen gadgets that creak and want lubricating
setter's reading: cooking vessels that need a coat of oil before use

explanation.walkthrough: Oiling suggests squeaky hinges, but it means the oil you heat before cooking food in shallow pans.
explanation.definitionFit: These shallow, long-handled cookware items are greased with fat or oil so food sizzles without sticking.

clue.text: Good vehicle

parts.note: surface reading: a reliable car or a fine form of transport
setter's reading: a carrier for goods, as a goods vehicle carries freight, here bought items

explanation.walkthrough: Good vehicle echoes a goods vehicle, a lorry; the answer carries goods of a humbler kind round a supermarket. Trolley is the British word for a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheeled supermarket cart is pushed around aisles to carry purchases, a vehicle for goods.

clue.text: Stir a dish of cereal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for a term in prison, stir being slang for prison
second meaning: oats cooked in milk or water

explanation.surface: An instruction to mix up a bowl of breakfast oats.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir looks like a cooking verb, but in British slang both stir and porridge mean prison time; doing porridge is serving a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is oatmeal boiled into a breakfast; as slang it means time spent in jail.

clue.text: Relate it differently when able to read and write

indicators.note: arranging something differently means putting these letters in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Telling a story in a new way once you have learned your letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A literate person has the basic skills of literacy, so can handle written language.

clue.text: Killed in action on the outskirts of southern besieged city

indicators.note: outskirts lie around the edge, so one piece wraps round the others

parts.note: a deed is an action
S is the abbreviation for southern
Troy was besieged by the Greeks for ten years

explanation.surface: Someone died in action outside a city in the south under siege.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Killed in action' reads as one phrase, but only 'Killed' is the definition; 'action' supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Destroyed can mean put down or killed, as when an animal is destroyed.

clue.text: The way wet weather causes tension

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Rainy weather making everyone stressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain is the pressure or stretching force on something, the same as tension in a rope.

clue.text: Make time for being healthy at home

parts.note: fit means healthy
in means at home

explanation.surface: Finding the hours to keep in shape without leaving the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit someone in is to find a slot in a busy schedule for an appointment.

clue.text: Fancy horse on the outside of front runner

indicators.note: being on the outside means one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a filly is a young female horse

indicators.note: front means we keep only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: opening letter of runner

explanation.surface: A horse racing alongside the leader, as if at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front runner' reads as the race leader, but splits into a selector and the word it works on.
explanation.definitionFit: Frilly clothes are ornate, decorated with ruffles, so they are elaborate rather than plain.

clue.text: Warm drink

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a fruit-flavoured beverage, diluted with water

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a hot beverage, but the two words are separate meanings; the drink is usually served cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes friendly, hearty relations; the noun is a sweet fruit syrup or liqueur.

clue.text: Detail on garment is a hit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the end of a sleeve
second meaning: a light blow with the hand

explanation.surface: A trimming on an outfit proves popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A hit' looks like a success, but it is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The turned-back band at a sleeve's end is a cuff; to cuff someone is to strike them lightly.

clue.text: How to blend in without right riding gear?

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: to stir up is to mix, a way to blend ingredients
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A question about mixing in, without any right way given, perhaps for a horse rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but in its old sense it means outside, so a letter goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup is the metal loop hanging from a saddle that supports a horseman's foot.

clue.text: The politician joined us on way back as well

indicators.note: going on the way back means this word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP has joined us on the journey home too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As well' looks like 'also', but 'well' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is a pit or reservoir where liquid collects, such as at the bottom of a mine shaft.

clue.text: Dance in brief lingerie

indicators.note: in means the answer sits within the run of letters that follows

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Dancing in skimpy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highland fling is a lively Scottish dance; a fling is also a brief affair, which fits the lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highland fling is a vigorous solo Scottish dance, so the word names a dance.

clue.text: Foolish person is unsophisticated, not backwards

parts.note: simple means unsophisticated

indicators.note: backwards means the word before it is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fool is naive, though not behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not backwards' looks like 'not slow', but 'not' is the word reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is someone lacking intelligence or common sense, an easily fooled dupe.
